investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T13:05–13:13Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), meaning the agent VM was never provisioned and the eval probe never reached the point of writing any output.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod remained Unschedulable for ~147 s, the eval probe timed out before a VM was assigned, and no contract evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pod node pool in the production-api environment, not an application code defect.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing peer-pods, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a specific node pool or label set that currently has no free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes do not carry that label.
[Possible] A quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the namespace or cluster level has been reached, preventing new allocations even if physical capacity exists.
[Possible] The 2 kata-capable nodes are in a degraded or cordoned state that prevents preemption victims from being evicted, as confirmed by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod'.
[Low likelihood] A recent deployment increased the number of concurrently running remote-agent VMs beyond the node pool's capacity without a corresponding scale-out of kata-capable nodes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: A kubectl describe nodes output showing kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable capacity is non-zero and available on the 2 eligible nodes would disprove the resource-exhaustion hypothesis.

A successful re-run of the remote-agent-create probe that produces orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent=true, and remoteState in {running, idle, ready} would confirm the issue was transient and has self-resolved.

Evidence that the pod was rejected for a reason other than resource exhaustion (e.g., image pull failure, admission webhook rejection, or missing secret) would shift the root cause away from node capacity.
Scheduler logs showing the 2 kata-capable nodes were cordoned or had taints that prevented scheduling for a reason unrelated to kata.peerpods.io/vm quota would refine the diagnosis.
A passing run of remote-agent-create concurrent with a failing run of an unrelated check would confirm the failure is isolated to the kata peer-pod pool and not a broader cluster or API outage.

Consider a stale-VM detection eval that lists all pods holding kata.peerpods.io/vm resources and flags any that have been running beyond a configurable TTL, helping identify leaked VMs before they exhaust pool capacity.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could never be scheduled, the runner never reached the state-polling step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~147 s), preventing the eval runner from creating an agent and therefore from collecting any required evidence. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

possibleCauses: PRIMARY — kata.peerpods.io/vm resource exhaustion on the 2 capable nodes: concurrent remote-agent workloads or leaked/stuck VMs from prior eval runs have consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for new pods.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, creating a combined capacity and topology constraint.

TERTIARY — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: if a previous createAgent() call did not clean up via withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903), a stranded VM could be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, blocking subsequent scheduling.

LOWER — Cluster under-provisioning: the cluster may have been sized for a lower concurrency of remote-agent evals than is currently being scheduled, and no auto-scaling or preemption policy is configured for kata.peerpods.io/vm nodes.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If the Kubernetes cluster shows available kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity (i.e., slots are not exhausted) at the time of the failure, the scheduling error message would be inconsistent with the cluster state and another cause (e.g., a misconfigured resource request in the pod spec) would need to be investigated.

If a re-run of the eval immediately after the failure succeeds and produces all four required evidence keys, it would suggest the exhaustion was transient (e.g., a concurrent eval run released its VM slots) rather than a persistent capacity deficit.

If the pod spec's node affinity/selector is found to be misconfigured such that no nodes in the cluster can ever satisfy it (regardless of VM capacity), the root cause would shift from capacity exhaustion to a pod spec misconfiguration.

If the withCleanup() path in run-status-probes.mjs is confirmed to always execute and no leaked VMs are found in the cluster, the VM leak hypothesis would be disproved, pointing instead to genuine under-provisioning or concurrent load.

If no-history data (previousRunCount=0, lastPassingAt=null) is explained by this being the first eval run ever, the absence of a regression signal would be expected and would not disprove the capacity diagnosis.

Extend the remote-agent-create eval to emit a distinct evidence key (e.g., schedulingErrorReason) when a pod fails to schedule, enabling the contract validator to distinguish scheduling failures from API or runtime failures.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Unschedulable: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 3 Remote-Agent Checks
investigations.summary: All three remote-agent checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-07T13:05–13:13Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not place the requested kata peer-pod because 2 nodes with the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource reported it as exhausted and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity/selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), meaning the agent VM was never provisioned and the eval probe never reached the point of writing any output.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes: 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity (resource quota exhausted or peer-pod slots fully consumed), and the other 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector rules. Because the pod remained Unschedulable for ~147 s, the eval probe timed out before a VM was assigned, and no contract evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) was ever written. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure / cluster-capacity failure localized to the kata peer-pod node pool in the production-api environment, not an application code defect.

possibleCauses: [Most likely] kata.peerpods.io/vm extended-resource slots on the 2 eligible nodes are fully consumed by existing peer-pods, leaving zero schedulable capacity for new remote-agent pods.

[Likely] Node affinity or node selector on the remote-agent pod spec restricts scheduling to a specific node pool or label set that currently has no free kata.peerpods.io/vm capacity, and the 4 remaining nodes do not carry that label.
[Possible] A quota or LimitRange on the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource at the namespace or cluster level has been reached, preventing new allocations even if physical capacity exists.
[Possible] The 2 kata-capable nodes are in a degraded or cordoned state that prevents preemption victims from being evicted, as confirmed by 'No preemption victims found for incoming pod'.
[Low likelihood] A recent deployment increased the number of concurrently running remote-agent VMs beyond the node pool's capacity without a corresponding scale-out of kata-capable nodes.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the eval pod could never be scheduled, the runner never reached the state-polling step, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was produced and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agents feature has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 nodes that carry that resource class. The remaining 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector. With zero schedulable nodes and no preemption victims available, every remote-agent pod creation attempt times out unscheduled (~147 s), preventing the eval runner from creating an agent and therefore from collecting any required evidence. This is an infrastructure capacity constraint, not an eval code defect. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence, so impact is scoped to the observability eval at this time.

SECONDARY — Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy, and those 2 nodes are also resource-exhausted, creating a combined capacity and topology constraint.

TERTIARY — VM resource leak from a prior eval run: if a previous createAgent() call did not clean up via withCleanup() (run-status-probes.mjs line 1903), a stranded VM could be holding the kata.peerpods.io/vm slot, blocking subsequent scheduling.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All 6 Cluster Nodes
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api on 2026-07-07 with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 2 kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes have insufficient VM capacity and the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod could not be scheduled, the eval runner never reached the point of creating an agent or collecting any evidence, leaving all 5 required contract fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote agent pod on any of the 6 available cluster nodes: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not satisfy the pod's node affinity or node selector constraints. The pod remained Unschedulable for ~145–147 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents VM pool in the production-api environment; it is an eval failure reflecting a real infrastructure constraint, but no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence to confirm a user-facing outage.

source-context.infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs:1910-1918: runner calls createAgent(args, track, 'remote', null, orgId) at line 1918; this call is the first step that triggers pod scheduling and is the point of failure.
possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource pool exhausted on the 2 capable nodes: concurrent workloads or a prior eval run consumed all available VM slots, leaving no capacity for the probe pod. Preemption was attempted and found no victims, ruling out a simple priority fix.

Secondary — node affinity/selector misconfiguration or drift: the 4 remaining nodes do not match the pod's required affinity/selector, meaning the schedulable surface is permanently limited to 2 nodes. If those 2 nodes are undersized for peak load, exhaustion will recur.

Tertiary — a prior eval run's cleanup did not release VM resources (e.g., a leaked agent pod holding a kata.peerpods.io/vm slot), reducing available capacity below the minimum needed for a new probe pod.

Lower confidence — transient node pressure (memory, CPU) on the 2 kata-capable nodes causing the extended resource to appear exhausted even if slots exist; would require node-level metrics to confirm or rule out.

After restoring capacity, re-run the three remote-agents probes to confirm recovery before closing this investigation.

whatWouldDisproveThis: If kubectl describe nodes shows kata.peerpods.io/vm slots are available and unallocated on the 2 capable nodes at the time of the failure, pool exhaustion is not the cause and a different scheduling constraint (e.g., taint, resource quota, admission webhook) must be investigated.

If the pod's node affinity/selector is found to match more than 2 nodes, the 4-node exclusion is not a structural constraint and may indicate a transient node condition (e.g., NotReady, taint) at the time of the run.
If a subsequent re-run of the probe succeeds without any infrastructure change, the failure was transient (e.g., a concurrent workload released VM slots) rather than a sustained pool exhaustion.

If the local-agent-runtime or local-agent-create checks are also failing at the same time, the failure may be broader than the kata.peerpods.io/vm pool and could indicate a cluster-wide scheduling or API server issue.

If no pods are found consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm resources at the time of failure, the resource exhaustion report from the scheduler may indicate a misconfigured node capacity advertisement rather than actual slot consumption.
followUpEvals: Add a dedicated eval check (e.g., remote-agent-vm-capacity) that queries the Kubernetes API for kata.peerpods.io/vm allocatable vs. allocated counts on all capable nodes and warns before exhaustion causes scheduling failures.
Add a check that detects leaked remote agent pods (pods in Running or Pending state beyond the expected eval window) to catch cleanup failures in the withCleanup path before they exhaust the VM pool.

Add a node-affinity-coverage check that verifies the number of nodes matching the remote agent pod's affinity/selector is above a minimum threshold (e.g., >= 2), alerting if node eligibility drops below the safe floor.

Consider a regression eval that runs remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, and remote-agent-runtime sequentially with a shared cleanup gate, so a scheduling failure in the first check prevents redundant scheduling attempts in subsequent checks.
